_comment: Hand-authorised rewrites (Ivan) for names OPSIN cannot read as extracted: the SPAN in the corpus stays verbatim, this only decides which structure the name stands for. structures.py loads these into REWRITE (a rewrite outranks the OCR repair). Each carries its reason. Added 2026-10-03.

Under as-indacene numbering 4-acetyl-1,1,6,6 (US 3,244,751) and 5-acetyl-3,3,8,8 (US 3,347,946) are the same molecule, so the numbering is consistent, and the held name is the other regioisomer; US4209543A distinguishes the crystalline prior-art isomer from the LIQUID 4-acetyl-3,3,8,8 compound. Claude's derivation, OPSIN-parsed; medium-high confidence, no external structure check (PubChem holds neither isomer). Approved by Ivan 2026-10-19

functional-class acetal name (IUPAC 2013 P-66.6.5.1.1: aldehyde, O-substituents, 'acetal'); the 6-dihydrolinalyl part is read from US4424146A itself: it makes compound (II) from 6-dihydrolinalool and ethyl vinyl ether with a trace of HCl (gives the 1-ethoxyethyl acetal on the alcohol O), compares it with the linalyl (I), tetrahydrolinalyl (III) and dehydrolinalyl (IV) acetals (so '6-dihydro' = only the 6,7 double bond saturated), and calls it an intermediate to 5,9-dimethyl-4-decenal (needs the vinyl group kept). PubChem (on Hetzner, 2026-10-20): 6,7-dihydrolinalool = 3,7-dimethyloct-1-en-3-ol (CID 86748); the reading is CID 163400 (CAS 84029-93-6), same InChIKey as OPSIN; the patent name is not among its synonyms. The patent's drawing (STR2) is not in our text. Checked by Joe 2026-10-20. Approved by Ivan 2026-10-20
